title: DNA extraction from mouse blood
author: Petra Schneider
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.86fhzbn
materials: Prepare reagents in kit only if opening a new MagMax 96-DNA multisample kit (Cat# 4413021), Add the appropriate amount of ethanol or isopropanol to the wash buffers (see table below) and mark the bottles clearly by crossing out the word “concentrate”, ticking the small checkbox and writing your name/initials and the date. Note: some of the bench-top reagents crystallise when the ambient temperature is low (below ~18°C). To combat this, set a heat block to 25°C before beginning and place the room temperature reagents on it until ready to use, remembering to mix well!
Open the BindIt software . Select ‘Your Kingfisher Machine’ from the drop-down ‘connect’ list to connect to your Kingfisher instrument ( note: connection has likely established automatically) .

steps.title: Dispense citrate saline
steps.instruction: Dispense 150 µL of citrate saline (0.85 % w/v NaCl, 1.5 % w/v trisodium citrate dihydrate) into each well of a 0.2 mL strip tube or 96‑well plate (one well per sample). Cover tubes with lids or seal the plate with the thick plastic film (not the optical qPCR film).

steps.title: Add blood sample
steps.instruction: Using glass capillaries, take 5 µL of mouse blood and dispense it immediately into the corresponding well of citrate saline. Repeat for all samples.

steps.title: Mix blood and saline
steps.instruction: Mix each well by pipetting up and down, then replace the lid; alternatively, replace the lid and mix by gently tapping the tube.

steps.title: Freeze or proceed
steps.instruction: Freeze the prepared samples at –20 °C for short‑term storage, at –70 °C for long‑term storage, or proceed immediately to DNA extraction.

steps.title: Gather plasticware
steps.instruction: Obtain 4 Kingfisher DeepWell (DW) plates (Cat# 95040460), 2 Kingfisher 96 (KF) plates (Cat# 97002540), and 1 DW tip comb (Cat# 97002534).

steps.title: Prepare Proteinase K mix
steps.instruction: In a sterile DNase/RNase‑free tube, combine 8 mL of Proteinase K solution with 42 µL of PK buffer (total ≈ 50 mL) for each sample well, then add 10 % extra volume to compensate for pipetting errors.

steps.title: Prepare bead mix
steps.instruction: In a sterile DNase/RNase‑free tube, mix 16 mL of DNA‑binding beads with 4 mL of nuclease‑free water (total = 20 mL) for each sample well, then add 10 % extra volume for errors.

steps.title: Dilute blood with ProK
steps.instruction: Use the prepared Proteinase K mix to dilute the 5 µL blood sample before transfer to the sample plate; this facilitates easier pipetting.

steps.title: Add bead mix to plate
steps.instruction: Dispense the prepared bead mix into the appropriate wells of the Kingfisher DeepWell plate according to the layout table.

steps.title: Centrifuge and remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate for 3 minutes at 4 °C. Using a clean pipette tip for each sample, remove the supernatant.

steps.title: Connect instrument
steps.instruction: Connect the Kingfisher instrument to the computer with a USB cable (usually already connected).

steps.title: Select BindIt protocol
steps.instruction: In the BindIt software, select the protocol (see step 22) and click the green ‘Start’ button.

steps.title: Load plates onto instrument
steps.instruction: Load the plates onto the Kingfisher turntable in the order shown in the layout table. Align the A1 well with the marked corner, press the instrument’s ‘Start’ button to confirm each plate, and allow the turntable to rotate as prompted.

steps.title: Execute dispense steps
steps.instruction: Once all plates are loaded, the run begins automatically. Follow the on‑screen prompts to add the correct reagents at each dispense step (grey cells in the machine protocol). The first dispense occurs ≈ 20 min after start; refer to the protocol table for approximate durations of subsequent steps.

steps.title: Remove plates and save report
steps.instruction: When the run ends (as prompted), remove the plates. Export and save the run details as a PDF (automatically opened) which records step start times and temperature logs. Do not discard plates yet.

steps.title: Inspect and seal elution plate
steps.instruction: Verify that liquid is present in the elution plate; if not, the run failed. Seal the elution plate with a freezer‑suitable plastic film (do NOT use optical qPCR film) and label it clearly.

steps.title: Store or dilute DNA extracts
steps.instruction: Freeze the sealed elution plate at –20 °C or use the DNA immediately for qPCR. For qPCR, dilute at least 1 volume of extracted DNA with 2 volumes of water to mitigate inhibitor effects.

steps.title: Discard used plates
steps.instruction: Discard all plates except the elution plate. Unused wells may be retained for future use, but must be filled with clean wells and any residual liquid removed before storage.

steps.title: Import optimized protocol file
steps.instruction: Import the file DNA5uLMouseBlood.bdz into BindIt (Layout tab: tip plate, sample plate, Wash 1, Wash 2_1, Wash 2_2, elution plate; Protocol tab: add the protocol).
